# fivenines Provider

Terraform provider for FiveNines server monitoring and observability platform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    fivenines = {
      source  = "Five-Nines-io/fivenines"
      version = "~> 0.6"
    }
  }
}

provider "fivenines" {
  api_key = var.fivenines_api_key
  # base_url = "https://fivenines.io" # optional
}

variable "fivenines_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Authentication

The provider authenticates with a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer fn_...`).
The **token**, not a user session, decides which organization Terraform manages.

The key can be provided in three ways, in order of precedence:

1. Provider configuration: `api_key = "fn_..."`
2. Environment variable: `FIVENINES_API_KEY`
3. A Terraform variable passed to the provider block

### The token must be write-scoped

Tokens carry `read` and/or `write` scopes, and `read` is a floor folded into
every token. Every create, update and delete this provider performs hits an
endpoint that requires the `write` scope, so a read-scoped token lets
`terraform plan` and every data source succeed and then fails the **first apply**
with a 403. Mint the token with the `write` scope.

A read-scoped token also cannot mint a write-scoped one — token creation is
itself scope-bounded.

### 401 and 403 mean different things

Both are terminal, and the distinction tells you which one to fix:

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | The **credential is dead**. | Mint a new token. |
| `403` | The credential is valid; the **action** is refused. | Grant the missing scope or permission. |
| `402` | The organization is suspended or its subscription is unpaid. | Settle billing. Reads keep working. |

The 401 is worth understanding because it is a fail-closed design rather than an
expired-token message. Membership is resolved from the **token's** organization,
never from the holder's most recent one: if the user who minted the token is no
longer a member of the organization it was minted for, every request answers 401.
That is deliberately not a 403 — the credential is dead, not the action forbidden
— and it is what stops a token following its holder from one organization to
another. A token belonging to someone who has left the org cannot be repaired by
adjusting permissions; it has to be replaced.

A 403 covers a read-scoped token attempting a write, an authorization refusal on
a resource the token's organization does not own, and demo-restricted
organizations.

Note that the 402 and the demo restriction apply to **writes only**. `GET`
requests are never refused by either, so `terraform plan`, `terraform refresh`
and data sources keep working for a lapsed organization.

### Rate limits

Limits are per organization, per minute, and plan-tiered: starter 300, pro 600,
business 1200, enterprise 2400 requests/minute. Every response carries
`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.

The provider retries a `429` automatically — up to 5 attempts, honouring
`Retry-After` and falling back to exponential backoff — so a brief overshoot is
usually invisible.

**The budget is shared with the FiveNines MCP server.** One counter serves both
surfaces, so an active MCP client competes with a Terraform run on the same
organization. If a large `terraform apply` hits sustained 429s, lower
`-parallelism` or stagger it against MCP activity.

### Quoting a request ID in support tickets

Every API response carries an `X-Request-Id`, and the provider attaches it to
every diagnostic it raises:

```
Error: Error creating instance

API error 422: [Display name can't be blank] (request_id: 9f1c4e2a-...)
```

That `request_id` correlates your failed apply with the server-side logs — quote
it when opening a support ticket.

## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) FiveNines API key (starts with `fn_`). Must carry the **write** scope: a read-scoped token answers 403 on every create, update and delete. Can also be set via the FIVENINES_API_KEY environment variable.
- `base_url` (String) FiveNines API base URL. Defaults to https://fivenines.io. Can also be set via FIVENINES_BASE_URL environment variable.
